data.title: Alkermes reinstated Buy at Truist on narcolepsy opportunity
data.description:
Truist Securities on Friday reinstated its coverage of Alkermes (ALKS) with a Buy recommendation and a $55 per share target, citing the potential of its lead orexin development candidate, alixorexton, against narcolepsy, a sleeping disorder.

Analyst Alex Nackenoff argued that alixorexton has already shown a superior clinical profile against narcolepsy type 1, and its existing data is sufficiently strong in narcolepsy type 2 compared with oxybates.

However, according to Nackenoff, its proof-of-concept data expected from a Phase 2 trial for another neurological sleep disorder known as idiopathic hypersomnia represents the key near-term catalyst for the stock.

“The readout expected toward the end of 2026 presents an attractive risk/reward opportunity; we believe positive data could translate to potentially +20% on the upside with minimal downside risk if negative,” he added.

While Takeda (TAK) is set to launch the first OX2R product branded as Orzeyful later this year, its opportunity is limited to NT1, according to Nackenoff. "Alixorexton has already demonstrated better efficacy vs. Orzeyful in NT1, and we feel the data is sufficiently strong in NT2 to deliver significant clinical benefit over oxybates,” the analyst added.

data.title: Ambarella may be seeing interest from a third bidder - report
data.description:
Ambarella (AMBA) is speculated to have garnered interest from a third bidder. 

There's speculation that one of the world's biggest AI chipmakers has entered a sales process for Ambarella (AMBA), according to traders who cited a Betaville “uncooked” alert that was circulating on Friday. 

The bidding war now consists of the unidentified chipmaker, NXP Semiconductors (NXPI), and Qualcomm (QCOM). Betaville last Friday said Qualcomm (QCOM) is speculated to be working with banks on a potential deal. The third bidder is described as bigger than NXPI and QCOM combined.

There's some speculation that the sales process is in its late stages and a deal could be announced in the coming weeks, according to Betaville.

Betaville first reported about Ambarella (AMBA) takeover speculation in late July. Ambarella jumped 16% on July 31 following the FT report that NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) was in talks to acquire the chip designer.

Shares of Ambarella pared much of an earlier decline on Friday.

data.title: Victoria's Secret is still in the early innings of a multi-year turnaround - Needham
data.description:
Needham started off coverage on Victoria's Secret (VSXY) with a Buy rating on its view that the retailer is only in the early innings of a multi-year turnaround.

Analyst Tom Nikic pointed to improvements to the Victoria's Secret (VSXY) management team, product assortment, and the marketing upside. Notably, Nikic and his team think the VSXY's EPS can double over the next five  years. 

As for the near term, strong quarter-to-date channel checks and lower promotions have Nikic calling Victoria's Secret (VSXY) a compelling beat-and-raise story.

Looking ahead, the company is seen as being a beneficiary of increased adoption of GLP-1 weight loss medicines as slimmed-down women shop for new clothes. All in, we view this as a compelling momentum name heading into 2027

Needham assigned a price target of $106 on VSXY based on a 16X multiple to its FY28 EPS estimate. The PT assumes mid-single-digit revenue growth the next two years and EBIT margin expansion. 

Shares of VSXY are up more than 60% on a year-to-date basis, but the Seeking Alpha Quant Rating is still flashing Strong Buy.

data.title: Nasdaq plunges 2% and these 15 names have led the downward decline
data.description:
Technology stocks came under broad pressure Friday afternoon as investors rotated away from growth-oriented names and the wider tech sector.

The broader tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) and the more concentrated Nasdaq 100 Index (NDX) both fell more than 2% during the session. The Nasdaq Composite declined a total of 2.1%, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.4%. The move reflected a clear risk-off tone concentrated in higher-valuation technology and growth companies.

Selling was widespread within the Nasdaq 100, where 73 of the index’s 100 constituents traded lower. CoreWeave (CRWV) led the declines, with the firm’s shares falling 12.6% and posting the steepest loss among index members.

data.title: Katie Zacharia has been ousted from her role as press secretary – report
data.description:
Current White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia has been ousted, according to three people familiar with the matter, New York Times reported Friday.

Zacharia has been under scrutiny due to how she presented her legal career and how she handled her press briefing. Her role as White House press secretary began on Oct. 12 and has reportedly lasted until Oct. 16.

President Donald Trump was questioned by reporters outside the White House and said, “Maybe the role is not for her.” He mentioned that he told her she did not have to stay in her role.

“I’m going to let her make the decision,” he said. “If I were her, I’d reconsider.”

Zacharia preceded Karoline Leavitt, who served the White House from January 2025 to August 2026.

The White House didn't immediately respond to Seeking Alpha’s request for comment.

data.title: Novartis halts mid-stage trial for kidney drug, Fabhalta, in lupus nephritis
data.description:
Novartis (NVS) has terminated a mid-stage trial for its oral Factor B inhibitor Fabhalta (iptacopan) in lupus nephritis, an inflammatory condition affecting the kidneys, because of strategic considerations, according to a federal database on clinical studies.

In an Oct. 15 update, the company said that it was no longer looking for enrollees for the two-part study, which evaluated the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of iptacopan (LNP023) with standard of care in 81 patients with LN.

Approved for multiple complement-mediated diseases, including primary immunoglobulin A nephropathy, Fabhalta generated roughly $505M in sales for the company last year, with over 150% YoY growth in Q4 on a currency-adjusted basis. Endpoints News first reported about the discontinuation.

The Swiss pharma giant has faced a string of late-stage trial setbacks lately, including for its RNA-based therapy del-desiran against a rare muscle-wasting disease called myotonic dystrophy type 1 in September. That came days after another late-stage trial failure for pelacarsen, a heart disease therapy it developed with Ionis Pharmaceuticals (IONS).

data.title: CoreWeave leads AI-related stocks lower during Friday free fall
data.description:
CoreWeave (CRWV) led AI-related stocks into the red during a Friday free fall affecting much of the tech sector.

CoreWeave shares had declined nearly 12% by early afternoon trading. The AI data center company has plunged 34% over the past 10 days. The declines reflect a growing concern among investors that the AI infrastructure boom could become increasingly difficult to finance, particularly if inflation keeps interest rates elevated and customers struggle to generate sufficient returns on their investments.

Fellow neocloud, Nebius, shed 11%. Its share value has collapsed nearly 33% over the past 10 days. IREN (IREN) declined 10%. It has collapsed 34% since October 6, following the same downward spiral as CoreWeave and Nebius over that time frame.

Hardware providers were also feeling the pain on Friday, as evidenced by the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) sinking 2.8%. Micron (MU) fell 4%, AMD (AMD) dropped 5%, and Intel (INTC) declined 4.9%. Nvidia (NVDA) held on better, inching down 1%. Its share value has lost 10% since October 6.

Networking and optical shares were sinking as well. Lumentum (LITE) declined 4%, Coherent (COHR) dropped 6% and Celestica (CLS) slid 3.5%.

While financing and fears of inadequate future revenue generation are prompting much of the sell-offs, the AI infrastructure buildout appears to remain unabated. Evidence for this appeared in TSMC's (TSM) latest quarterly earnings report, which was released on Thursday.  

Interestingly, analog and mixed-signal semiconductor stocks have remained more resilient. Texas Instruments (TXN) inched up 0.4% on Friday. Analog Devices (ADI) was relatively flat, and Onsemi (ON) was down 1%. Although these have all declined since October 6, the drops have not been as pronounced.  

Software was not exempt from Friday's bleeding. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV) had declined nearly 5% by afternoon trading. 

A pullback in AI-related stocks has weighed on the broader market this week, with memory chip stocks among the hardest-hit segments as investors reassessed the sector's recent performance. SK Hynix (SKHY) fell 5.7% on Friday.

data.title: American Airlines Q3 preview: What guidance says about fuel-cost risks
data.description:
American Airlines (AAL) heads into its October 22 earnings report with a key challenge: turning strong revenue growth into better profitability.

Wall Street expects a loss of $0.33 per share on revenue of $16.20B, while analysts have issued 18 downward EPS revisions and no upward revisions over the past three months.

The company’s third-quarter guidance highlights the pressure. American Airlines expects revenue to rise 16%–19% YoY, with available seat miles increasing 3%–5%.

However, it forecasts an adjusted loss of $0.70–$0.10 per share and a 2.5%–4.5% increase in non-fuel unit costs. Its fuel-price assumption was approximately $3.75 per gallon, based on the July 21 forward curve.

The full-year outlook also reflects the fuel burden. The company now expects adjusted EPS between a loss of $0.65 and a profit of $0.65 per share, citing higher fuel costs. Further increases in fuel prices could put additional pressure on earnings.

The second-quarter results showed why revenue growth has not translated into stronger profits. Revenue climbed 16.3% YoY to a record $16.74B, but operating expenses climbed 22.9% to $16.29B.

Fuel expense surged 83.3% to $4.88B, while operating income fell 60.7% to $446M. Adjusted EPS dropped to $0.15 from $0.95 a year earlier.

The company also recently warned that elevated jet fuel prices would push its third quarter results below the midpoint of guidance. 

The airline is also trying to strengthen customer loyalty. Its new cash-and-miles booking option gives AAdvantage members more flexibility, while a planned Starlink rollout across its mainline fleet could improve the onboard experience from 2027.

Despite these initiatives, the company continues to face a profitability gap with larger rivals Delta Air Lines (DAL) and United Airlines (UAL). Investors will be looking for signs that management can control costs and convert revenue growth into stronger earnings.

On the market side, the shares traded near $11.99 on Friday, down 21.17% year to date, while the S&P 500 (SP500) gained 13.13%.

Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating for the stock is 'Hold' at 3.21, with A+ grades for valuation and growth but a D+ grade for earnings revisions.

data.title: Meta Muse continues to see increased adoption, though overall rates are low: BNP
data.description:
The strong interest in Meta Platform's (META) Muse artificial intelligence agent does not seem to be slowing down, BNP Paribas said on Friday.

Citing third-party data analysis, the investment firm said the app, which overtook OpenAI's (OPENAI) ChatGPT at the top of the App Store, has generated more than 10.4M downloads so far, BNP analyst Nick Jones said in a note to clients. Downloads peaked on day 12 of the release and have since stabilized in an upward trend, the analyst added. Jones has an Outperform rating and an $885 price target on Muse.

“While Muse Wonder is mainly targeting enterprises and developers, it will also power Meta Muse, initially for paid subscribers, which could help increase adoption and engagement,” Jones wrote in a note to clients. “Compared with other AI platforms, Muse’s early U.S. downloads surpassed Sora and ChatGPT, which is not surprising given its massive install base for Instagram, WhatsApp, and Facebook.”

Delving deeper, Jones said engagement for Muse is still early, and users are "predominantly" men, and younger people have “relatively low adoption” of the app. As such, it's unlikely to be a threat in the near-term to vertical marketplaces due to “still-nascent” adoption and a few other issues. 

“In terms of monetization, as of now, Meta is charging partners small transaction fees. Muse is free for the basic tier and offers monthly subscriptions for higher usage to maximize adoption and engagement,” Jones added. “But we believe long-term monetization remains a question mark for investors—we see a path where advertising could be compelling as engagement builds.”

Events that investors will need to pay attention to include how well OpenAI's Dots (which is believed to be geared towards the enterprise) does, as well as when other companies such as Google (GOOG) (GOOGL), SpaceX (SPCX), and others launch their AI agents, Jones added.

data.title: Microsoft is the only hyperscaler not forecast to dip into negative FCF in the next year
data.description:
Microsoft (MSFT) stands alone among major hyperscalers as the only one not forecast to dip into negative free cash flow territory over the next twelve months, according to BofA Global Research Equity and Quant Strategy.

Amazon (AMZN), Alphabet (GOOGL), (GOOG), Oracle (ORCL), and Meta (META) are all expected to fall into negative free cash flow by 2027, with BofA Global Research projecting these hyperscalers' next-twelve-month free cash flow estimates will drop below negative $25,000 between 2026 and 2028.

 

 

 

The outlook isn't entirely bleak for the sector, according to BofA Global Research, which expects hyperscalers' free cash flow to shift from negative to positive by the second half of 2027 as AI-related revenue growth accelerates and AI capital expenditures decelerate.

However, the research firm warns of significant risk: AI capex has surprised to the upside by a much wider margin than revenue—50% versus 20% this year—meaning 2027 expectations imply a marked shift in trend.

 

 

 

BofA Global Research's estimated compute demand through 2030 implies approximately $10T of spend, roughly $2T above current forecasts.
